items.title: why the periodic set-up fails: diagnosis on processors
items.task: Diagnose, on processors and without changing source, why the periodic set-up of package periodic_threshold fails. Evidence so far: card job 4799 (run A-20261121-131600-02b5d41): both members were stopped by the guard of release core-v0.5 (conformal factor not positive), P0L at t = 4.8 and S1L at t = 15.1, and in both the norm of the Hamiltonian constraint jumps by about 1e4 at t = 2.5 (the lead's reading run A-20261121-203120-eaba95f with its figure; the lead's latest message to core in tracks/A-emd-pbh/outbox/; periodic_threshold/README.md, JOURNAL.md and decks). Prediction first, for every run. (1) Reproduce the jump in the smallest, coarsest set-up that shows it on processors (threaded build: scripts/cpu_run.sh with the release executables of core-v0.6 in scratch/core/exe/core_nrpic_v06/, at most 6 cores; look at uptime first). (2) Locate it: where in the box and in which variables the constraint first grows (dumps around t = 2.5), and which event coincides: a regrid or the edge of the refined region, the lapse relaxation, a step limit, the first shell crossing, the deposit across levels, the guard itself. (3) Test each candidate with a run in which it could fail: with and without <z4c> lapse_leak; uniform mesh against refined; halved step; deposit shape and filter; against the earlier periodic runs of this track that did not fail (what differs). (4) Verdict: the cause if a run shows it, otherwise what is excluded; a minimal reproducing input with its command, posted to core (outbox message of type request with run ids); and what Track A can run in the periodic set-up meanwhile. Figures looked at; README.md; JOURNAL.md. Do not touch the queued chains or the sequencer of this owner.
